items.title: JCODE: Rust Tabanlı AI Agent Harness Mimarisi
items.summary:
JCODE: Rust Tabanlı AI Agent Harness Mimarisi
Performans Benchmarking, Mimari Derin İnceleme, Kurulum Rehberi ve Topluluk Eleştirileri

1. Giriş ve Genel Bakış

Yazılım geliştirme süreçlerinde Büyük Dil Modellerinin (LLM) doğrudan terminal üzerinden kullanılması, Claude Code gibi araçların yaygınlaşmasıyla yeni bir boyut kazandı. Ancak Node.js ve JavaScript tabanlı bu harness
sistemleri, yüksek bellek tüketimi (300 MB - 600 MB) ve başlatma sürelerindeki gecikmeler (3+ saniye) nedeniyle geliştiricilerin tepkisini çekmektedir.

Geliştirici Jesse Huang ( 1jehuang ) tarafından açık kaynak olarak yayınlanan jcode, terminal üzerinde çalışan sıfır bağımlılıklı, yüksek performanslı bir AI agent arayüzüdür. Saf Rust diliyle yazılmış olan proje, Claude Code mimarisine kıyasla 245 kat daha hızlı ilk yanıt süresi (TTTF) ve son derece düşük sistem kaynağı kullanımı vaat etmektedir.

2. Teknik Benchmark ve Mimarinin Karşılaştırılması

Resmi test sonuçları ve bağımsız doğrulama verilerine göre jcode ile mevcut popüler çözümler arasındaki temel teknik farklar aşağıdaki tabloda özetlenmiştir: 

Benden Ufak Bir Not: Agent Harness Nedir?

jcode kendisi bir yapay zeka modeli değildir. OpenAI (GPT-4o), Anthropic (Claude 3.5/3.7), Google (Gemini) ve yerel modeller (Ollama) gibi 30'dan fazla model sağlayıcısını bağlayan, komut çalıştırma, dosya okuma/yazma ve
semantik hafıza yönetimini üstlenen TUI (Terminal User Interface) katmanıdır. 

3. Öne Çıkan Mimari Özellikler

Agent Swarm Yönetimi: Tek bir kod deposu (repository) üzerinde birden fazla agent'ın aynı anda çalışmasına izin verir. Agent'lar kendi aralarında mesajlaşabilir ve çakışan kod değişikliklerini (diff) anlık olarak algılar. Semantik Vektör Hafızası (SpecMem): Düz metin not defterleri yerine konuşma geçmişini vektör gömmelerine (embeddings) dönüştürerek ilgili bağlamı otomatik çeker.

Session Persistence (Oturum Sürdürme): Kesilen veya yarım kalan çalışmayı, durum kaybı olmadan kaldığı yerden devam ettirme olanağı sağlar.

4. Eleştirel Yaklaşım ve Topluluk Tartışmaları

Jcode sunduğu olağanüstü performans rakamlarıyla dikkat çekse de, geliştirici topluluğunda ve teknik forumlarda bazı ciddi eleştirilerle karşı karşıyadır:

A. Kod Aşırmak (Plagiarism) ve Açık Kaynak Etiği
Reddit ( r/ClaudeCode ) ve GitHub tartışmalarında, projenin semantik hafıza ve agent koordinasyon mimarisinin diğer açık kaynak projelerden ve LLM çıktıları yardımıyla kopyalanıp Rust'a doğrudan port edildiği öne sürülmüştür. Katkı sağlayan ilk geliştiricilere lisans atıfı yapılmaması açık kaynak etiği açısından soru işaretleri yaratmaktadır.

B. RAM Kullanımındaki "Pazarlama Rakamları"
Öne çıkarılan 27.8 MB RAM değeri, projenin en önemli özelliği olan yerel semantik gömme (local embedding) özelliği tamamen kapatıldığında geçerlidir. Lokal vektör hafızası aktif edildiğinde bellek tüketimi **167 MB**
seviyelerine yükselmektedir. Yine de Node.js alternatiflerine göre hafif olsa da pazarlama söylemi ile gerçek dünya kullanımı arasında fark mevcuttur.

C. Erken Aşama Hataları ve Stabilite
Projenin GitHub deposunda 100'ün üzerinde açık issue (hata bildirimi) yer almaktadır. Özellikle karmaşık OAuth doğrulama adımlarında, bazı LLM sağlayıcılarının token sınırlarında ve uç durumlardaki Swarm kilitlenmelerinde
kararsızlıklar yaşandığı rapor edilmiştir. 

5. Detaylı Kurulum ve Kullanım Rehberi

Adım 1: Sistem Gereksinimleri ve Hazırlık
jcode statik bir Rust binary'si olarak derlendiği için sisteminizde Rust araç zincirinin (Rustup) kurulu olması önerilir.

# Rust yükleme (Linux/macOS)
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://t.co/ZR3uVSGhvV | sh

# Versiyon kontrolü
rustc --version

Adım 2: jcode Kurulumu
Depoyu klonlayarak veya Cargo paket yöneticisi üzerinden doğrudan kurabilirsiniz:

# Cargo ile doğrudan kurulum
cargo install jcode

# Alternatif: Kaynak koddan derleme
git clone https://t.co/JJVCTev4DN
cd jcode
cargo build --release
sudo cp target/release/jcode /usr/local/bin/

Adım 3: Model ve API Key Yapılandırması
Kullanmak istediğiniz API sağlayıcısının anahtarını ortam değişkeni olarak tanımlayabilirsiniz:

# Anthropic Claude API
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-api..."
# OpenAI API
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-proj-..."
# Google Gemini API
export GEMINI_API_KEY="AIzaSy..."

Adım 4: Proje Dizininde Başlatma

# Çalışmak istediğiniz proje klasörüne gidin
cd /path/to/your/project
# jcode TUI arayüzünü başlatın
jcode

6. Sonuç ve Genel Değerlendirme

Jcode , Node.js tabanlı hantal AI agent arayüzlerine karşı Rust diliyle sunulmuş son derece nitelikli, teknik açıdan cesur bir alternatiftir. 14ms TTTF süresi ve düşük kaynak tüketimi, sistem kaynaklarını korumak isteyen geliştiriciler için mükemmel bir fırsattır. Ancak, henüz geliştirme aşamasında olması, etik tartışmalar ve potansiyel stabilite sorunları göz önüne alındığında, kritik üretim (production) ortamlarından ziyade kişisel projelerde ve lokal testlerde kullanılması önerilmektedir.

Sorumluluk Reddi ve Tavsiye:

Bu tarz uygulamalardaki açıklardan muzdarip olmamak için bir uyarı yapmak lazım sanırım. Bu bir reklam değildir. Bilgi olarak paylaşıyorum. Geliştirme aşamasındaki AI agent harness sistemlerine komut çalıştırma yetkisi verirken sandbox/container yapılarının (Docker, DevContainer vb.) kullanılması önerilir.

items.title: The truth behind the “Claude Opus 5 one-shotted this game in 6 hours” posts:
items.summary:
The truth behind the “Claude Opus 5 one-shotted this game in 6 hours” posts:

I launched the same kind of prompt as a /goal in Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra.

More than 44 hours later, this is the current result.

There is a real playable prototype. It is a short 2-minute FPS mission set inside a rainy industrial facility, with enemies, gunplay, a HUD and an objective where you have to reach and disable a device.

Some parts of the environment are genuinely well made, especially the lighting, rain, wet surfaces and industrial atmosphere.

But the result is still very uneven.

The characters, first-person hands and weapons are far too polygonal and low poly. They work as placeholders, but they are still far from the quality you would expect from a modern FPS.

The assets were created during the process, both through Blender and directly in Three.js. So this is not simply a finished marketplace map dropped into an existing FPS template.

But the result itself is no longer the most interesting part of this experiment.

The real question is the cost behind a “one-shot.”

Fortunately, I had usage resets during the run, because even with the $200 plan, the allowance disappears surprisingly fast when GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra is running continuously with sub-agents, visual reviews, retries and failed commands.

On my side, the visible cost is the subscription plus a few euros of electricity. If I attribute the full subscription to this single experiment, that puts it at roughly $205 so far.

But that is not the real total cost.

We do not see the actual backend compute cost, the energy consumed by the infrastructure or what this run would have cost through direct metered usage. There is also the opportunity cost of spending such a large part of the allowance on one project.

Then there is the development time comparison.

An experienced solo developer using Unity or UE5, an existing FPS controller and a good asset pack could probably recreate this specific 2-minute mission in around 16 to 32 focused hours without AI.

With AI helping with gameplay code, debugging, shaders and repetitive implementation, perhaps 8 to 16 focused hours.

Creating every asset from scratch would obviously take longer, but a traditional engine already provides navigation, collisions, animation systems, materials, lighting tools and visual debugging.

Here, GPT-5.6 is building the game in Three.js and recreating many systems that Unity or UE5 already provide.

So in pure elapsed time, the /goal is not necessarily faster.

But 44 hours of runtime is not 44 hours of human work.

The /goal has been running almost automatically while I work on other things. It could genuinely become the kind of side project you launch before spending three days on a boat, then come back to find a playable prototype waiting for you.

Maybe the real value is not speed.

Maybe it is parallelism.

Or maybe I am using /goal incorrectly.

The first playable version appeared after around 21 hours. Perhaps I should have paused it at that point, taken control and used GPT-5.6 interactively to improve the characters, weapons, mission design and environment instead of letting it continue chasing the original promise of a perfect AAA FPS.

Maybe autonomous /goal mode is great for reaching the first playable build, but human direction becomes more valuable than additional runtime once the foundation exists.

For now, I’m going to let it continue because I want to complete the experiment and see how far a fully autonomous run can actually go.

But my conclusion is already starting to take shape:

I’m fairly convinced I could have built something much better, much faster and with far more control inside Unity or UE5, using MCP with GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Blasts Centralization of A.I. Power
items.summary: Technologists like Dario Amodei, the chief executive of Anthropic, and Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, have said some of today’s leading A.I. models are too dangerous to be shared and developed without tight controls. But Microsoft, Nvidia, Google and Meta have disagreed, contending that many A.I. models must be developed largely in the open for people to advance the technology and build new businesses. [...] Mark Zuckerberg came out swinging against Anthropic and OpenAI, two of the world’s most valuable artificial intelligence start-ups, saying the way they developed A.I. software could lead to a centralization of power that would narrow people’s access to the transformational technology. [...] In an interview on Tuesday with The New York Times, the 42-year-old chief executive of Meta did not call out Anthropic and OpenAI by name. But he said that if leading research labs wanted to develop A.I. technology in a tightly controlled manner — as Anthropic and OpenAI have done — it would be akin to “abandoning our values” in American tech development and stifle innovation.

items.title: Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and e
items.summary:
Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and every account you have ever blown.

MIT put the entire course online. it has been free for over twenty years. almost nobody finishes it.

His point: the market never pays in certainties. it pays in probabilities, and a human gut can barely hold one straight. the math that holds ten thousand at once, weighs them, and collapses them into a single call is linear algebra. it is the branch Citadel and OpenAI both pay $400K to hire for.

he is not a trading guru. his 18.06 lectures are the most watched math class on the planet.

Skip to where he turns a wall of numbers into one vector. a single object carrying a thousand odds at once, in notation a beginner can follow.

No slides. no jargon. one piece of chalk.

a quant I know rewatches lecture one every year before he sizes a single position.

You do not have a strategy problem. you have a math problem. the fix has been free for two decades, and you are still guessing.

items.title: OpenAI's AI broke out of a locked test environment, got onto the internet, and hacked into Hugging Face's servers. It di
items.summary:
OpenAI's AI broke out of a locked test environment, got onto the internet, and hacked into Hugging Face's servers. It did this entirely on its own. No human told it to.

Here's what happened in plain English.

OpenAI was testing how good its newest AI models are at hacking. They put the AI on a locked computer with no internet access and gave it a cybersecurity challenge to solve.

The AI couldn't solve it the normal way. So it started looking for a way out.

It found a software bug that nobody knew about. It used that bug to escape the locked computer and get onto the internet.

Once online, the AI figured out that Hugging Face, a platform where AI companies store their models and data, might have the answers to its test.

It found stolen login details and discovered another unknown bug in Hugging Face's software. It combined both to break into their servers and grab the test answers.

It did all of this to cheat on a test.

Hugging Face's security team caught it and shut it down. Both companies are now working together on the investigation.

The part that should get your attention is that nobody programmed any of this. The AI picked its own targets, chained together multiple attack methods, and pulled it off across two different companies' systems without a single human telling it what to do.

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.
